\begingroup\singlespacing\footnotesize
\noindent\textit{Notes:} \emph{This table's baseline and the $d_Z=5$ column of
\cref{tab:supp-app-ladder} are the same specification, and what separates their
numbers is the cross-fitting draw.} Both are the five-control set on the same
$983$ counties, at the same initial condition, step, stopping rule
$\tau_{\mathrm{DP}} = 0$, budget $\bar m = 15$ and five folds; they differ in
how many partitions are averaged over, ten in the ladder against six here, and
in the seed, which is why the baseline reports $30$ fold solves against the
ladder's $50$. \emph{The gaps between the two tables are therefore a stability
check and not a sensitivity.}
\emph{The two tables differ in which coefficients they print and in which
standard error.} This table prints a fixed set, the constant with population and
the high-school share, pinned rather than reselected because the high-school
share holds the second slot over per capita income by $0.0024$ in $|t|$, a
margin of $0.0917$ per cent the cross-fitting draw alone can overturn; and
it prints the state-clustered standard error alone, where the ladder prints the independent
one in parentheses and the clustered one in brackets, so a figure here is read
against the ladder's bracketed column. Per capita income, which
this table does not print, is $0.5363$ $(0.2013)$ against the ladder's $0.5732$
$[0.1947]$; in units of that column the three gaps are a third of a
standard error at population, a fifth at per capita income and a thirtieth at
the high-school share. \cref{tab:supp-app-diag} Panel D puts the cross-fitting
share of the standard error at $0.218$.
Every arm is the five-control set on the $983$-county
sample except ``All $989$ counties'', which restores the six dropped in
\cref{tab:supp-app-sample}, and each varies one tuning constant from the
baseline and nothing else. The coefficients of $\hat\theta$ that are not
printed are estimated in every arm.
``Median $\hat m$'' is the realised Landweber--Fridman stopping
index across that arm's fold solves; the last two columns count the solves that
returned their initial condition and those that reached the cap, so an
arm that looks stable while those counts are high is stable for the wrong
reason. \emph{The $X$-coordinate row returns no estimates}: outside the
pooled-rank coordinate $\hat\pi$ is not bounded away from zero, and the
adjoint divides by it. What fails is the sample reference density: C1(ii)
bounds the population $\pi$ away from zero and is untouched here. That row prints what the bandwidth ladder found,
and the three items in it read as follows. Of $31$ rungs only $2$ leave
$\hat\pi>0$; those two span $h_x\in[1.410,1.485]$ in $\mu$g/m$^{3}$, an interval
$5.1$ per cent wide about its own midpoint and a factor of $5.00$ below the
$7.42$ that the rule of thumb returns, which is the bandwidth every other arm
runs at; and ``rank $23$ of $31$'' is the same ladder in the pooled-rank
coordinate, which is feasible at $23$ rungs where this one is feasible at $2$.
Even on those two rungs $\hat\pi$ is negative on the dense grid in $120$ of
$120$ builds. What fails is the lower endpoint and not
the $428.1$ outlier: the guard minimum sits between the $0.25$th and $0.38$th
percentile of $X$, whose smallest value is $0.0$ and next $7.84$, and trimming
the largest counties raises the failures from $5$ of $120$ builds at $k\leq2$ to
$18$ at $k=5$ and $10$. One row carries both coordinates because min--max is an
exact affine image of $\mu$g/m$^3$ to a relative $7.07\times10^{-14}$; the rows
they printed separately differed through the L'Ecuyer stream each drew, and so
through the cross-fitting partition. Panel C of \cref{tab:app-phi} reports
the same failure for $\hat\varphi$. The
comparison block reports just-identified linear
instrumental variables on the same sample and the draft alternating estimator,
for which no standard error is computed. Source: \texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_03\_robustness.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_robustness.tex}; run object
\texttt{quality\_reports/application/app\_tsp\_robustness.rds}.
\par\endgroup
\end{landscape}

\begin{tablenotes}\scriptsize
\item \textit{Notes:} Chay--Greenstone county panel, $n=983$, at the headline
control set $d_Z=5$, with the instrument entered as its four trigger cells. Panel
A evaluates $\hat\varphi(x)-\hat\varphi(x_{0.5})$ at
eleven percentiles of the pooled distribution of $\{X_1,X_2\}$, normalised at
its median $x_{0.5}=58.0\,\mu$g/m$^3$; the ``TSP'' column is the particulate
level in $\mu$g/m$^3$ at that percentile, and the last two columns count the
counties within $\pm5\,\mu$g/m$^3$ of it in each period, so a row supported by
few counties is visible as such. The bootstrap columns summarise $99$
replications that resample counties with replacement and re-run the
regularisation in each, holding $\hat\theta$ fixed; the envelope is the $5$th
and $95$th percentile of the
replications at that level. \emph{The envelope illustrates variability and is
not a confidence set. No coverage is claimed for it and none is computed}, which
follows \citet{centorrinofeveflorens2019} for the same estimator on the same
equation. Panel B records the design and what it returned: $\hat m_\varphi$ is
the realised Landweber--Fridman stopping index and $\bar m=60$ the cap, which is
set from the instrument's cardinality at $15$, $30$ and $60$ for
$\mathsf L=2$, $3$ and $4$. \emph{Every solve reported here terminates at that
cap}, because the discrepancy rule runs at $\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}=0$ and the
patience equals the cap, so the rows recording $\hat m_\varphi$ describe the
budget and not a selected index. The two rows counting replications at
$\hat m_\varphi=1$, where a replication would have returned its initial
condition unchanged, are zero for that reason and not for a favourable one, in
the subsample comparison as in the resample. ``S.d.\ of the anchor across
resamples'' is the standard deviation across replications of the weighted pooled
median each curve is re-anchored at, in $\mu$g/m$^3$ and not in log points.
\emph{The cap is a calibration constant and not the $\bar m_n$ of
\eqref{eq:cap}}, which Panel A of \cref{tab:sim-stopping} measures at
$3.95\times10^{10}$ to
$8.76\times10^{11}$, a factor of $7.32\times10^{8}$ to $2.78\times10^{9}$ above
the $\hat\delta_n^{-2}$ it is meant to dominate; the two are different objects
and only the first bounds the runs reported here. Panel B's last block re-estimates $\theta$ inside each of $25$
draws rather than holding $\hat\theta$ fixed, and the resulting band on those
same draws is narrower, $0.0388$ against $0.0412$; the block's last row
counts the $\theta$-step fold solves that reach the cap, at the median over the
five folds. The multiplier arm's counterpart to Panel A, which the text compares
this envelope with at the ends of the support, is \cref{tab:supp-app-phimult},
and \cref{tab:supp-app-bootcompare} carries the two schemes' summary statistics side
by side. Panel C recomputes the whole
normalised curve in one other strictly increasing coordinate of $X$,
$\mu$g/m$^3$, and returns nothing: $\hat\pi$ is not bounded away from zero
there, so the estimator is infeasible in that coordinate, and a min--max
rescaling shares the row as an exact affine image of it. \emph{No hypothesis of
this article is violated by that}: what fails is the sample reference density the
engine builds, and the conditions here are stated on the population $\pi$. The baseline
row is filled in pointwise over the $60$-point grid: ``Max $|\Delta|$'' and
``RMS $\Delta$'' are in log points, the two ``/SD'' columns divide them by the
bootstrap standard deviation at the same point, ``Steps up'' counts the grid
steps on which the curve rises, and the last column is the band width on $25$
paired draws. A strictly increasing reparameterisation leaves
$\vdagger\circ T^{-1}$ structural and $\theta_\dagger$ unchanged, so what fails
is the estimator at this sample and not the model; the magnitudes reported in
Panel A and drawn in Figure 1 of the article are those of the pooled-rank
coordinate. Source:
\texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_05\_phi\_band.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_phi.tex}.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}

information while holding duplication at zero. Three rows record the stopping index. \emph{Retained with $\hat m_\varphi=1$}
counts the replications that returned the initial condition, where the Landweber
step never fired; \emph{Retained with $\hat m_\varphi=\bar m$} counts those that
ran to the cap; and \emph{Stopped before the cap} is the complementary share.
Under this configuration the first is zero and the second is every replication
in all four columns, for the reason \cref{tab:app-phi} gives, so those rows
describe the budget and not a selection. The bootstrap columns draw $99$ replications and
the subsample columns $24$, so a difference of one replication is worth
$1.0$ and $4.2$ percentage points respectively. \emph{None of these bands is a
confidence set and no coverage is computed for any of them.} Source:
\texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_06\_phi\_mult.R} and
\texttt{app\_tsp\_05\_phi\_band.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_phi\_boot\_compare.tex}.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
\end{table}

% caption or no caption, and the \captionof above has already numbered this
% table and claimed the label. Without this line the number is swallowed and

% it, and 44/45 now that three Section 6 floats have arrived ahead of it.
\addtocounter{table}{-1}
\endgroup
\begingroup\singlespacing\footnotesize
\noindent\textit{Notes:} The multiplier arm of \cref{tab:supp-app-bootcompare}, at
the eleven percentiles \cref{tab:app-phi} reports for the pairs arm.
Chay--Greenstone county panel, $n=983$, headline control set $d_Z=5$, instrument
entered as its four trigger cells, $\hat\theta$ held at its full-sample value.
Panel A's columns are those of \cref{tab:app-phi} and are formed the same
way: $\hat\varphi(x)-\hat\varphi(x_{0.5})$ at percentiles of the pooled
distribution of $\{X_1,X_2\}$, re-anchored in each replication at that
replication's own weighted pooled median, with the envelope the $5$th and $95$th
percentile of the replications at that level. \emph{The envelope illustrates
variability and is not a confidence set. No coverage is claimed for it and none
is computed}, exactly as for the pairs envelope. What differs between the two is
the scheme: one weight per county, $w_i$ i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ normalised to
mean one and shared by both of that county's periods, against a resample of
counties with replacement. $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ matches the first two moments of the
multinomial weights the resample induces, so the two perturb the sample equally
hard and differ in what they perturb, mass rather than support; all $983$
counties and all $983$ distinct values of $X$ are present in every replication
here. The coordinate map is the one further departure. It is held at its
full-sample value, which a with-replacement resample cannot do, so the
second-stage grid is identical across replications and differences between
curves are differences in the estimate rather than in where it was evaluated.
What that conditioning omits is measured rather than asserted: the last two rows
of Panel B rebuild the map from the weighted empirical CDF on the same first
$25$ draws, and the band on those draws is $0.0352$ with the map rebuilt against
$0.0356$ with it held, so holding it overstates the width by $0.0004$ there
rather than understating it.
\emph{No verdict is reported, and none is available.} The rule fixed before the
run judged this scheme against the pairs scheme on the stopping-index
distribution alone, on the share of replications at $\hat m_\varphi=1$, the share
at the cap, and the median index, because a band can be narrow either because
the procedure is stable or because it collapsed to its initial condition and only
that distribution separates the two. At $\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}=0$ the discrepancy
branch never fires and the patience equals the cap, so every solve that returns
returns $\hat m_\varphi=\bar m=60$; the index is a constant, all three criteria
are then satisfied by construction for any data in either arm, and they
discriminate nothing. The script records no verdict rather than one read off an
unfailable test, and the three rows of Panel B that report the stopping index
carry no information under this configuration, which is what their
$[\,60,60\,]$ range says. \emph{Neither envelope is uniformly the narrower.}
Against the pairs envelope of \cref{tab:app-phi} this one is wider at the
$5$th percentile, at the $70$th and at the $80$th, $90$th and $95$th, and
narrower from the $10$th to the $30$th and at the $60$th; at the $40$th and the
$50$th it is wider by less than $0.0006$, taken on the unrounded envelope bounds
and not on the four digits printed, which give exactly $0.0006$ at the $50$th.
It is therefore the wider of the two at seven of the eleven levels and the
narrower at four, a split that is the same on the printed digits and on the
unrounded bounds, so a single summary of the two widths does not carry to the
level at which it is read, and Section 6 of the article reads that pattern off
this table.
\Cref{tab:supp-app-bootcompare} reports each band's median width over the
$60$-point grid and the two schemes' other outcomes side by side. The remaining
rows of Panel B record the draw: $99$ replications, all $99$ returning a finite
curve, no errors and no non-finite curves; ``S.d.\ of the anchor across
replications'' is the standard deviation across replications of the weighted
pooled median each curve is re-anchored at, in $\mu$g/m$^3$; and ``Weight s.d.''
checks the draw itself against the value $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ implies. Source:
\texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_06\_phi\_mult.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_phi\_mult.tex}.
\par\endgroup
\end{landscape}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\begin{threeparttable}
\caption{The operator's squared norm in three coordinates, and what the default
Landweber step does in each}
\label{tab:supp-app-opnorm}
\footnotesize
\input{../tables/app_tsp_opnorm}
\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} $\|A\|^{2}$ is the squared norm of the composite map
$q\mapsto\mathfrak w\cdot\{h_q(X_2)-h_q(X_1)\}$, $h_q'=q$, obtained by the same
$30$-step power iteration the estimator itself runs to set its relaxation; the
reported values are stable to six significant figures across four starting
seeds. It is the \emph{squared} norm, which is the quantity
\eqref{eq:normconst} bounds: the iteration converges for a step below
$2/\|A\|^{2}$, the third column. The fourth column divides the default step
$0.5$ by that bound, so a value above one is a step the convergence condition
forbids, which is the $\mu$g/m$^3$ row and no other. The last column reports what
the default step produces in each coordinate, namely the largest fitted
$|\Delta\hat\varphi|$ over the sample, in log points of property value. \emph{Only the $\mu$g/m$^3$ coordinate violates the bound}, and it is the
only one whose fitted curve leaves an economically interpretable range. The
``Iterations run'' column is printed so that the last column can be read as a
comparison: all three coordinates are still iterating when the count runs out,
so what separates them is the magnitude and not the stopping. That count is a
diagnostic choice and not the application's cap, which C4 sets from the
instrument's cardinality at $15$, $30$ and $60$.
Source:
\texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_07\_opnorm.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_opnorm.tex}.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
\end{table}

holds on the $\varphi$-step grid}
\label{tab:supp-bdrylayer}
\let\tabular\longtable
\let\endtabular\endlongtable
\input{../tables/sim/sim_thm_rootn_bdrylayer}
% longtable.sty's \LT@array opens with \refstepcounter{table} UNCONDITIONALLY,

\addtocounter{table}{-1}

\begingroup\singlespacing\scriptsize
\textit{Notes:} The two hypotheses the $\varphi$-step arm makes about its
$x$-smoother, measured on DGP-A's pooled design $\{X_{1i}\}\cup\{X_{2i}\}$ at
ten sample sizes from $125$ to $181{,}019$. The table sets the configuration
shipped through 2026-08-15, which smoothed at $h_x=n^{-0.20}$ with a kernel
renormalised to unit mass at each design point, beside the current one, at
$h_x=n^{-0.40}$ with the family of \cref{lem:bdryfam} at $p_K=8$; ``D11'' in the
panel heads is the former and ``C3'' the latter. The spanning header dates the
two blocks of Panel A, below which each panel names its own configurations, and
no header repeats on a continuation page. Panel A counts the design points
within $3h_x$ of an endpoint, the layer C3(ii) governs. The old bandwidth put
every pooled point inside it up to $n=2{,}828$ and $51.93$ per cent of them at
$n=181{,}019$, so the interior kernel was never the operative one anywhere on
the arm's grid; the new one holds $48.55$ per cent at $n=500$, against the $884$
of $1{,}966$ pooled points, $44.96$ per cent, that Section 6 of the article
realises on the county panel (\cref{tab:supp-app-bdrymom}, notes). Panel B is the
departure from \eqref{eq:truncmom} at each order $j$, worst over design points,
each configuration on its own quadrature; the third column grows the node count
as $N\propto n^{0.40}$ and is the rule the current arm uses. Panel C reports
\eqref{eq:xsmoothbias} realised and the ratio (P-g) requires to be $O(1)$,
$\sup_{\mathcal X}|\varphi_{h_x}-\vdagger|/(h_u\hat\delta_n)$, at $3$ to $25$
draws per $n$, and Panel D fits that ratio's slope in $\log n$ against two
standard errors; the slope is compatible with $O(1)$ only if it is at or below
zero by both. \emph{Section 5 of the article claims the arm now runs
on-hypothesis; this is the evidence, and the claim is about the slope and not
the level.} Under the old configuration the ratio climbs monotonically from
$3.13$ to $8.09$ at a slope of $+0.125$ whose regression standard error is
$0.003$, so the climb is not a Monte Carlo artifact and no re-reading of the
constants removes it. Under the current one the slope is $-0.813$ at a
regression standard error of $0.173$ against a Monte Carlo one of $0.001$, which
is the diagnostic saying one line is the wrong model for a curve that falls and
then flattens; the article reports the plateau, $9.6\times10^{-7}$ averaged over
the last four sample sizes, rather than the fitted rate.

Panel E decomposes the move in the cap \eqref{eq:cap} into the legs of
$\bar m_n\propto c_C\mathsf c_2^{4}h_x^{-1}h_u^{-2}$ at $n=500$, $2{,}000$
and $8{,}000$. \emph{It is an independent recomputation of Panel C$'$ of
\cref{tab:sim-stopping}, not a second assertion of it, and the two reach the $h_u$ leg
by different routes.} Panel C$'$ takes the total from the $\varphi$-step arm's
realised $\bar m_n$ over $300$ replications and recovers the $h_u$ leg as the
residual against the three derived legs; Panel E measures $h_u$ on this arm's
own draws, $25$ at each of the three sizes, and multiplies the four legs out.
The derived legs agree exactly, the constants at $8.974\times10^{4}$, the
bandwidth at $n^{0.20}$ and the family at $1.00$; the $h_u$ leg, the only
quantity the two routes compute differently, agrees to within $0.68$ per cent,
and the totals inherit that and agree to within $0.71$ per cent,
$3.458\times10^{5}$ here against the $344{,}503$ printed there at $n=500$. Two
routes agreeing to that tolerance check the arithmetic and the realised
$\bar m_n$ in a way neither table does alone, which is why both are printed.
Monte Carlo standard errors in parentheses. Source:
\texttt{scripts/simulations/sim\_thm\_rootn\_bdrylayer.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/sim/sim\_thm\_rootn\_bdrylayer.tex}; run object
\texttt{quality\_reports/sim/sim\_thm\_rootn\_bdrylayer.rds}.
\par\endgroup

\caption{The frontier at each rung of the control-set ladder}
\label{tab:supp-app-feasibility}
\footnotesize
\input{../tables/app_tsp_feasibility}
\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Chay--Greenstone county panel, $n=983$, first differenced.
Rows are the four rungs of the control-set ladder of
\cref{tab:supp-app-ladder}, indexed by the number $d_Z$ of differenced controls
entered: an intercept alone, five core hedonic demand shifters, those plus five
demographic variables, and all twenty-two usable controls. The first three
columns are the frontier read in the primitives of the article's
\eqref{eq:frontier}, $r>d_Z(2\mu+1)/\{2(2\mu-1)\}$ with $r$ the H\"older
smoothness of the propensity score and $\mu$ the source index, evaluated at
three values of $\mu$; they are properties of the condition and of $d_Z$ alone
and involve no estimate. The remaining columns are evaluated at
$(\mu,r)=(2,\tfrac83)$, which is the frontier-clearing configuration of the
article's Section 5: $\kappa\alpha$ with $\kappa=2\mu/(2\mu+1)$ and
$\alpha=r/(2r+d_Z)$, against the $\tfrac14$ the frontier requires; $\delta_n$ at
this $n$; the leading Step-4 product $\sqrt n\,\delta_n^{2}$; and the sample
size at which that product would fall below one. The last two of those are the
two rows Panel D of \cref{tab:supp-app-diag} repeats. \emph{``Verdict'' reports
the frontier and nothing else.} It is ``inside'' at the intercept-only rung
because any $r>0$ clears a threshold of zero there, and that rung is
nevertheless unavailable: A4(ii) requires $d_Z\ge1$, and at $d_Z=0$ the
propensity exponent is $\alpha=\tfrac12$ exactly, at which the sieve-entropy
condition admits no integer sieve dimension and \cref{thm:rootn} is vacuous
there. So the frontier is met at no control set the assumption block also
admits, which is the statement Sections 6.4 and 7 of the article read off this
table. At the three rungs that do satisfy A4(ii) the budget never falls below
one at any $n$, because $\tfrac12-2\kappa\alpha>0$ there and the product grows.
Every entry is a deterministic function of the design and of $n$; no Monte Carlo
standard error attaches to any of them, and nothing here is estimated from the
outcome. Source: \texttt{scripts/application/app\_tsp\_01\_diagnostics.R}; table
\texttt{paper/tables/app\_tsp\_feasibility.tex}; run object
\texttt{quality\_reports/application/app\_tsp\_diagnostics.rds}.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
\end{table}
